After reading the image and converting it to the proper RGB format, it performs the rotation in two distinct steps: cv2.getRotationMatrix2D(): This function computes a mathematical 2x3 transformation matrix needed to rotate the image. It requires three parameters: the exact center pixel coordinates to act as the pivot point (width / 2, height / 2), the angle of rotation in degrees (45 degrees counter-clockwise), and a scale factor (1, meaning the image stays its original size) . cv2.warpAffine(): This function takes the calculated rotation matrix and actually applies it to the image's pixels, mapping them to their new locations. It requires the target dimensions (width, height) so it knows how large of a canvas to draw the newly rotated image on. Finally, the newly rotated image is displayed intine using Matplotlib. Note that because the image canvas size remains the same, the corners of the rotated image will get cut off, and the empty space left behind wilt be filled with black pixels.
